name: com.auspiceoracle/bazi
title: Auspice — Chinese Classics & Tao
description: Verified passages from the Chinese classics for hard decisions, plus a true-solar-time BaZi chart.

tools.name: cast_chart
tools.description: Casts a BaZi (Four Pillars) chart from a birth date, time and place, applying true solar time correction first (daylight saving, longitude and the equation of time). Returns the four pillars with hidden stems and Na Yin, the day master, the season, and the luck-cycle sequence, plus a comparison chart cast from raw clock time that shows what a calculator skipping the correction would get wrong for this birth. The result has a formatted scroll (the display form) and the same data as structured fields. Runs on the production Auspice Oracle engine (conventions at auspiceoracle.com/en/method). Deterministic calendar facts only: no strength verdicts, favorable elements or interpretation. The output is calendar data only and is not a forecast; the luck-cycle sequence is a charting convention, not a timetable of fortune, money, property, relationships, health or decisions. What the chart can describe is temperament and tendency.

year.description: Birth year, Gregorian calendar (engine ephemeris covers 1900–2100)

lang.description: Language of the rendered output — pass the language the user is conversing in. Defaults to 'en'.

gender.description: Sets luck-cycle direction (a charting convention, not an identity statement)

tools.name: personality_sketch
tools.description: Step 1 of 2 for a personality sketch from a BaZi chart. Casts the chart and returns the chart facts plus a fill-in template with three sections (象 image / 里 beneath / 行 practice), each grounded only in the returned facts and within stated limits (no strength verdict, favorable elements, Ten Gods or luck-cycle reading). Step 2 is compose_sketch, which frames the three filled sections into the finished sheet.

tools.name: compose_sketch
tools.description: Step 2 of 2 for a personality sketch: takes the three sections written from the personality_sketch template (image / beneath / practice, in the same lang) and returns the finished framed sheet, with the fixed mirror line, limits, quotation, link and signature assembled server-side. Fills that stray into out-of-scope territory (Ten Gods, strength, favorable elements, luck cycles) are returned as an error naming the terms, so they can be rewritten and resubmitted.

tools.name: tao_lens
tools.description: Passages from the Chinese classics for a situation someone is in: weighing a decision, a change, waiting, loss, conflict, overwork, comparing themselves with others, fear, or starting something. Takes one or two themes (not the user’s own words) and returns two or three passages from the Daodejing, Zhuangzi, Analects, Mencius and the Yijing (read as text; nothing is cast), each with the original Chinese, a literal English translation, the chapter and a link to the public-domain source, a one-line reading and one open question. Every quote is checked character by character against Wikisource. No birth data needed. Reflection only: the result contains no advice and no predictions. Not suited to crises or to medical, legal or financial questions.

themes.description: One or two themes that fit the situation: decision, change, waiting, loss, conflict, overwork, comparison, fear, beginning

exclude.description: Passage ids already given in this conversation, to get different ones

tools.name: chinese_zodiac
tools.description: Returns the Chinese zodiac animal and year pillar for a birth date under both rules in use: the BaZi rule, where the year changes at Lichun (the start of spring, around February 4), and the Lunar New Year rule used by most zodiac sites and calendars. For births in January and early February the two often disagree; the result says whether they do, gives the exact Lichun moment and the Lunar New Year date for that year, and explains the difference. Also returns the day master for the same date (the day pillar, which BaZi reads as the person). Birth time and time zone are optional and matter only for a birth on Lichun day itself; without them the result gives both possible answers. Deterministic calendar facts, 1900–2100.

hour.description: Birth hour, 24-hour clock (optional; only decides a birth on Lichun day)

minute.description: Birth minute (optional; 0 if only the hour is given)

timeZone.description: IANA time zone of the birthplace, e.g. 'America/New_York' (optional; Beijing time if omitted)

lang.description: Language of the rendered output — pass the language the user is conversing in. Defaults to 'en'.

tools.name: day_pillar
tools.description: Returns the BaZi day pillar (stem-branch of the sixty-day cycle) for a Gregorian date, or for today if no date is given. For a birth date this is also the day master, the centre of a BaZi chart, which needs only the date. Includes the stem element, branch animal, hidden stems, Na Yin, the day-master image and motto, the month and year pillars, the solar term in effect and the lunar date, plus a note on the 11 pm day-change convention. Deterministic calendar facts from the Auspice Oracle engine, 1900–2100; no interpretation or prediction.

timeZone.description: IANA time zone that decides which date 'today' is when no date is given (default Asia/Shanghai)

lang.description: Language of the rendered output — pass the language the user is conversing in. Defaults to 'en'.
